Definition: burning, i.e. (figuratively) poisonous (serpent); specifically, a saraph or symbolical creature (from their copper color)
BiblicalUsage: Saraph is burning — the fiery serpent in the wilderness, and the burning ones who stand above the throne. When the serpents bit Israel in the wilderness, God told Moses to set a fiery serpent on a pole, so that everyone bitten who looked upon it would live; and the same word names the seraphim, each with six wings, covering face and feet and flying, one of whom carried a live coal from the altar to the prophet's lips. It is the same fire in both places: the wilderness that held fiery serpents and scorpions, and the throne room where burning ones worship.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the burning ones show me that God's holiness is not cold or distant; it burns, and it comes close. The same fire that judged the bitten in the wilderness healed the prophet's lips at the altar, and the serpent lifted on the pole became the way to live. What I take from this is that God does not leave His fire at a distance — He sends it to cleanse, and He lifts up the cure where the bitten can see it.
